svg.aria-label: Figure 1.3: Sumerian Clay Artifacts Field Guide showing five artifacts: Beveled-Rim Ration Bowl, Hollow Clay Bulla and Tokens, Carved Stone Cylinder Seal, The Kushim Barley Ledger Tablet, and Tamper-Proof Clay Contract Envelope
svg.text: Figure 1.3: How Sumer Turned Wet Mud Into Rations, Memory, and Law
Five clay artifacts excavated in southern Mesopotamia—showing how bookkeeping grew from grain bowls to court contracts.
Found by the thousands near Uruk temples;
scholars think crews got daily barley in them.
Clay tokens tracked sheep, oil jars, and grain,
sealed inside a hollow clay ball (bulla)
so nobody could secretly alter the count.
Carved stone cylinder rolled on wet clay
to leave a continuous raised picture-signature
that cracked visibly if tampered with.
Wraps it in a thin clay
